print_parts.supports: Build with top face on bed; support only captive-nut recesses if needed.
Four M3x16 screws pass through the 4 mm feet and 4 mm cover spacers into captured body nuts. Seat the servo on the lower ledges. Fit four M3 nuts in the upper pockets before the cap.

Four M3x10 screws secure the cap to the saddle. Upper lips contact the nominal case top before the ears close: the ears retain 0.3 mm tightening travel. Stop when the case is retained without distortion. Slots allow 0.45 mm lateral adjustment each way.

Seat directly on the metal horn outer face. Four M3x6 screws with 0.5 mm washers of at most 6.0 mm outer diameter sit in the 1.5 mm deep counterbores and engage 2.0 mm of the 2.5 mm metal flange. Verify this stack with the real horn. Fit the spline retaining screw before the cradle. Four M3 nuts enter the bottom pockets for the cradle feet.

Print flat on X=-4.5 rear face. Fit four nuts from the phone side for the rear feet before inserting the landscape phone. Both short ends have USB clearance at the phone midpoint. Rear camera openings remain clear at both ends. Top and bottom contact occurs near the corners, with central edge relief for the power and volume buttons. Measure actual buttons, cameras and the parked charging plug before assembly.
Attach with two M3x16 screws from the screen side into the outer post nuts. The landscape bare phone has 0.5 mm end clearance and 0.55 mm screen clearance.

Insert the landscape bare phone from above, then attach this cap with two M3x16 screws. The corner-seat top gap is 0.5 mm. The central long edge has button relief; front retention covers the outer corner regions, with both rear ends open for the camera.
Print on a broad Y side. Fit two M3x10 screws downward through the foot into hub nuts, then two M3x10 screws from behind into the frame nuts. Check tips remain behind the phone cavity.
